text:
Alex G: heads up — multiple hosted-inference customers reporting a sharp spike of 502/504s from SFO edge starting ~08:05 UTC. CS has 3 escalations opened. Gateway logs show upstream resets + auth retries. anyone oncall?

CS Rita: paste from customer A logs: `502 Bad Gateway` repeated, `upstream connection reset` in the gateway, and some requests show `401` then immediate retry -> `429` from auth service. customer shared a sample request id: req_8a1c4f2b. attaching their short capture link (s3://redwood-support/sfocustA_pcap). billing impact potentially duplicate token counts from client retries.

Maria L: @Alex @Oncall Joe I see microburst patterns on sfo-edge egress interfaces correlating with packet retransmits and RTOs. netstat shows `connection reset by peer` and tcp_retransmits jumping. metrics: egress_if_rx_drop spike 08:04:50–08:07:10. Looks like upstream link microbursts (short-duration) causing packet reorder and upstream svc timeouts.

Oncall Joe: taking lead. BGP sessions are stable, no withdraws, but interface gx1 shows tx queue spikes. traceroute from sfo-edge -> model-host: `* 40ms 120ms 40ms * 120ms` (intermittent high latency then drop). Running `tc qdisc` shows backlog spikes. Planning temporary egress path shift for affected prefixes to secondary IX.

Alex G: CS Rita — give customers repro steps. Use this curl and include x-request-id header:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
     -H "x-request-id: test-req-123" \
     -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Also ask them to run `curl --trace-ascii trace.txt` and attach. We need three samples across different clients to correlate.

CS Rita: sent to customers. one customer did the curl and got 4/10 requests 502, backoff retries lowered error count. They uploaded `trace.txt`. forwarding to infra.

Infra-SRE Bot: auto: created incident INC-8421 for alert sfo-edge-5xx-spike. auto-escalation to network team.

Oncall Joe: mitigation actions in flight: 1) push routing policy to steer affected prefixes to secondary peering, 2) enable temporary extra retries (backoff) in gateway for hosted endpoints to reduce visible 5xx, 3) enable local KV cache fallback for heavily used model endpoints to reduce upstream calls. Pushing configs now.

Maria L: short-term kernel tweak on sfo-edge to reduce tx queue pressure: setting `net.core.netdev_max_backlog=5000` and lowering `tcp_rmem` min to reduce bursts. I'll deploy as a canary on 2 nodes first.

Alex G: note on billing: customers that retried aggressively saw duplicate ingestion counts in billing pipeline. Finance @ops to reconcile potential double-charge window 08:04–08:10. CS will offer temporary credits until reconciliation.

CS Rita: customer A confirmed error rate fell back to baseline ~08:12 after routing shift. They accepted temporary credits and closing their support escalation; asked for postmortem.

Oncall Joe: ops: routing shift completed at 08:10, monitoring shows stable egress with 5xx back to baseline. Will keep watch for 2h then remove temporary kernel knobs if stable. Incident INC-8421 marked mitigated; keeping thread open for provider confirmation and billing follow-up.

Maria L: next steps for postmortem: gather pcap slices, egress interface counters, provider side logs and ask provider for link optics report (possible short-duration fiber microburst). Also add an automated rollback to primary path if we see sustained lower latency for 10m.

Alex G: thanks all :thumbsup: — CS to file customer postmortems and finance to reconcile billing. If provider confirms physical microbursts, we'll add an ops runbook for similar events.

Oncall Joe: closing from ops POV at 08:30 UTC, incident will remain in monitoring. incident id INC-8421.
